steps.visual_purpose: A side-by-side display of five candidate findings, one column ordered by analytical interestingness and one ordered by relevance to the stakeholder's decision, making the contrast between the two ranking principles visible.
Show a finding statement alongside a correctly framed recommendation for the same situation, making the structural difference between restating data and stating an action visually obvious.

Show a contrast between a weak opener that buries the purpose in lengthy background versus a strong two-sentence context section that immediately level-sets the reader on what the report covers and why it was done.

tiles.title: Sample Size, Effect Size, and Statistical Significance

steps.visual_purpose: Side-by-side display of two groups of estimated lift values — one cluster tight around 10% (large sample) and one scattered widely around 10% (small sample) — making visible that small-sample estimates vary more around the true effect than large-sample ones.

A strip of twenty-five horizontal confidence intervals built from different samples around p = 0.88, with one interval visibly missing the true population proportion line — making the repeated-sampling interpretation and the interval-capture misconception concrete.

A number-line diagram showing a 95% confidence interval as a shaded band, with two scenarios side by side: one where the null value (p0 = 0.333) falls inside the interval (fail to reject) and one where it falls outside and below the interval (reject, conclude lower) — making the contrast between the two textbook examples immediately visible.

tiles.title: Defining the Question and Planning the Workflow

steps.visual_purpose: Show a vague complaint on the left ('deliveries feel slow lately') beside the scoped business question on the right ('Which delivery zones are missing the delivery-time target, and by how much, over the last quarter?'), with the three scoping decisions (which orders, which measure, which unit of comparison) annotated between them.

A two-column side-by-side showing 'Data source: SQL database → Retrieval method: SQL query via pandas.io.sql' alongside 'Data source: Excel workbook → Retrieval method: read_excel()', making the source-to-tool mapping visible at a glance.

A linear six-stage flow (Scope → Retrieve → Clean/Model → Analyze → Visualize → Communicate) with a back-arrow from any later stage to Scope, a quality-check indicator spanning all stages, and a callout at the Model stage noting that relationships connect the orders and drivers tables.

Show the two-phase structure (design → analysis) with an annotation at each phase indicating what is produced: an analytical plan (with iteration arrows) in the design phase, and a decision log alongside the analytical outputs in the analysis phase.

Show a raw analytical finding (e.g. a table of zone delay percentages) alongside the finished narrated summary paragraph, so the learner can see how the same information is transformed into an audience-facing story with context, finding, and recommendation.

Show the two-part structure of the final capstone step: (1) a documentation layer capturing decisions, assumptions, and QA checks at each prior stage, feeding into (2) a delivery layer comprising the summary pack, visualizations, and presentation — making clear that both parts together constitute the evaluable deliverable.
